text: Collect-then-reserve keeps every per-app vector (with growth slack) live next to the reserved list, so the peak is about 2-3x the data and the >=40 MB drop is not achieved.
evidence: Design Fix 1: count first from AbiCache (abi_node_counts via a shared load_abi helper), reserve_exact, then ingest and extend one app at a time; ABIs are cached anyway (abi_ingest.rs:~212).

text: ingest_abi grows its per-app vectors from Vec::new() by doubling; Base Application's vector can be a large slack-carrying block.
evidence: Design Fix 2: ingest_abi presizes objects/routines with Vec::with_capacity from the same exact counts.

text: The planned >=8 MiB logger must also hook realloc (the 51 MB doubling is a realloc) and record the new size; net-delta accounting hides the old+new overlap.
evidence: Design Measurement tool: alloc, alloc_zeroed AND realloc logged by new requested size (old size for realloc), with old+new transient noted in the run notes.

text: Backtraces inside the allocator need a reentrancy guard and lazy symbol resolution; the probe's release profile has no debug info, so build_dep_nodes may not appear as a frame.
evidence: Design: thread-local guard, unresolved capture resolved at print, debug = "line-tables-only" in the probe profile, census-hook phase marks as fallback attribution.

text: 'Largest single allocation inside build_dep_nodes' is ambiguous: ABI parse and sort-scratch allocations also fall in that phase.
evidence: Metric defined: the largest Vec<RoutineNode>/Vec<ObjectNode> buffer (size a multiple of size_of, backtrace through build_dep_nodes or the dedup); all other >=8 MiB allocations in the phase are listed.

text: Corpus fidelity is unproven: GUID grouping keeps one version per app, so fewer than 263 may be ingested, and the probe README uses a different .alpackages.
evidence: Hard gate: the master f3f0b304 run must reproduce the 51,032,576-byte Vec<RoutineNode> realloc before any code change; the run records ingested SymbolOnly units and size_of::<RoutineNode>().

text: The shrink_to_fit rationale was false: the old code left capacity = the pre-dedup length, so shrinking is an extra realloc, not parity.
evidence: Design Fix 3: no shrink_to_fit; in-place retain_mut on the presized list leaves the same capacity as before.

text: The planned dedup test projection (ids + flags) cannot see same-id alias reordering or context intersection, and its layout does not force the verdict iterator to stay aligned.
evidence: D1 asserts a literal ordered projection with param_sig_key, a distinguishing payload, preproc_context, both flags and AbiParams; Drop entries are placed before collapsed/aliased runs; breaks (a)-(d) include skip-context and advance-only-on-keep.

text: An end-of-loop debug_assert catches only an over-long iterator; zip would hide a mismatch.
evidence: assert_eq!(verdicts.len(), routines.len()) before the loop and .expect() on each next() inside it.

text: Goldens may not exercise step 2b over several SymbolOnly units, so count-first ordering would be unpinned.
evidence: D2 interleaves >=2 seeded units with >=2 unseeded failing units (distinct cache keys) and asserts abi_ingest_errors order, parse_count = 2 and dep_routines.capacity() = raw count; the reorder break targets the error order (node order is fixed by the step 4 sort and step 1 AppRefs); skip-one-unit targets contents.

text: The dedup helper is also called by assemble_program_graph for workspace routines; the design did not say so.
evidence: Design Fix 3 states it: the workspace path gets the same in-place behaviour, with no change in meaning.

text: If results were collected, each should be pooled (share_strings) before being retained.
evidence: Moot under count-first: no result is retained; the per-app loop pools and extends exactly as today.

text: A wrong count shows only as capacity, never as contents, so neither D1 nor D2 pins the count-first change.
evidence: D3 asserts abi_node_counts == (objects.len(), routines.len()) and capacity == len over all four load paths (hit, load, no path, failing path); D2 asserts dep_routines.capacity() = the raw pre-dedup count. Round 3: D3 path 2 is now an UNSEEDED real tiny .app built with test_apps::build_app, asserting parse_count 1 after counting and 1 after ingestion.

text: The >=40 MB build-peak drop only follows if the build peak lies in the step 2b/dedup phase.
evidence: Pass criterion is the OVERALL build peak drop >= 40 MB (the issue's); the census-hook phase peaks are diagnostic only; a shortfall with a >=40 MB phase drop is recorded under Not delivered as an operator decision, never a pass.

text: A lazily initialised or destructor-carrying thread_local can allocate inside GlobalAlloc.
evidence: Guard declared thread_local!{ static IN: Cell<bool> = const { Cell::new(false) } }; log records pushed only while the guard is set.

text: The Design read the 40 MB target against the phase peak while the Acceptance row and the issue use the overall build peak.
evidence: Same fix as N2: the overall build-peak drop is the pass criterion; phase peaks diagnostic; shortfall goes to Not delivered.

text: capacity == len can pass by coincidence when a fixture's count lands on the doubling growth path (e.g. 4+4=8), and D2's capacity check already holds on master's with_capacity(len) dedup.
evidence: Final form: D2's object total is 5 (off ObjectNode's 4/8 growth path) and debug_assert_eq!s in build_dep_nodes pin lengths and capacities of objects/routines/dep_meta against the counted totals; a full revert to Vec::new() fails (build.rs:285, (8,8,4) vs (5,7,2)).

text: D3's break (a) (count only the first object's routines) cannot fail if the fixture puts all routines on one object.
evidence: D3's fixture spreads its routines over at least two ABI objects (e.g. 2 + 1 = 3), keeping the total off the growth path.

evidence: Now pub(crate).

text: The in-place dedup keeps incoming growth slack that master's with_capacity(len) rebuild trimmed (workspace assemble_program_graph path; embedded-mode step 2), retained for the snapshot/DepCache lifetime; the comment claiming parity was false.
evidence: build.rs dedup records pre_len and shrink_to(pre_len) after retain_mut = master's capacity (no-op on an exact list); the false parity comment is corrected. D4 pins it: a with_capacity(8) list of 4 ends at capacity 4; dropping shrink_to fails D4 (8 vs 4).

text: Step 2b's reserve_exact is a no-op when step 2's doubling slack already covers the ABI total, so 'reserve once, exact' does not hold in mixed snapshots.
evidence: Step 2b no longer reserves on its own: one with_capacity(total) before step 2 covers source summaries + SymbolOnly ABIs, so the reservation cannot be swallowed by step-2 slack.

text: Step 2 still grows objects/routines by doubling across source-dep summaries although every length is already known.
evidence: build_dep_nodes counts objects/routines/routine_meta over the in-memory summaries plus abi_node_counts before step 2 and allocates objects, routines and dep_meta once; step 2 and 2b append without growth.

text: ingest_abi builds a per-app Vec the caller then copies with extend (a ~10 MiB transient for Base Application).
evidence: Beyond #84's ask (reserve once + dedup in place); changes ingest_abi's signature and needs a slice share_strings. Filed as a discovery with its measurement (the 10,655,232 B per-app buffer in the after run). Recorded under the ledger's ## Discoveries (item 1) with the measurement.

text: After the fix the build peak sits at step 4's stable-sort scratch buffer (len/2 RoutineNodes, 13.5 MB).
evidence: A separate optimisation (unstable sort on (id, index) or an index permutation) with its own order-preservation proof; filed as a discovery with the after-run evidence. Recorded under the ledger's ## Discoveries (item 2) with the measurement.

text: Each SymbolOnly unit is looked up in AbiCache twice (count pass, ingest pass).
evidence: 263 extra lookups (four short key Strings + an uncontended mutex each) against ingesting 120k routines; no measurable cost, and threading the Arcs through would widen ingest_abi's API for nothing.

text: D2's capacity check covers only a fixture without step-2 routines and cannot see retained slack.

text: Exact capacity() asserts are not guaranteed by std.
evidence: Same as R2: std's with_capacity/reserve_exact are exact today and the tests say so in a comment; an exact check is the only way to pin the reservation, and a future std change would surface loudly, not silently.
